a6685.en:
Articles on the fisheries agreement

Opposition wants more benefits and sustainability in the Fisheries Agreement
The PAICV declared itself in favour of the fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union, but argued that it must be accompanied by studies proving the sustainability of fishery resources and guaranteeing that there is no negative impact on the activities of national fishermen. The UCID, for its part, stated that the country could obtain greater benefits if measures were implemented to strengthen the national fleet. The MpD, meanwhile, argued that the agreement is based on the principles of transparency, sustainability and equitable sharing of benefits.

Minister clarifies the limits of maritime sovereignty in the fisheries agreement with the EU
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Jose Filomeno Monteiro, denied that the fisheries agreement with the EU harms Cabo Verde, explaining that the EEZ is not equivalent to territorial waters and that the passage of foreign vessels is permitted under international law. As he stressed, the agreement covers migratory species and guarantees financial compensation for the fisheries sector and coastal communities.

With foreign aid retreating, a new attitude is required
A Financial Times newspaper poll published earlier this week revealed that 60% of Americans agreed with the freeze on American international aid under the direction of USAID, taken by Donald Trump and implemented by Elon Musk. Only 12% of those polled disagreed with the idea that significant amounts of aid funds are wasted on corruption and administrative costs, to the detriment of those truly in need.

Biosfera's calculation on the fisheries agreement ignores additional fees and investments, says Government
The Government clarified today that Biosfera's claim about the sale of tuna caught in Cabo Verdean waters at "13 escudos per kilo" results from a simplified interpretation of the financial compensation under the Fisheries Agreement with the European Union (EU). According to the Executive, that figure does not reflect the reality of the agreement, since it disregards additional fees paid by European vessel owners, as well as indirect investments in monitoring, sustainability and the development of the national fisheries sector.

"The problem is not the fisheries agreement but rather its application in practice" - president of Apesc
The president of the Association of Fishing Vessel Owners of Cabo Verde (Apesc) considered that the problem does not lie in the fisheries agreement that the country has been renewing with the European Union, but rather in its practical application.

Sao Vicente: Minister of the Sea says "the new fisheries agreement was the one that was possible"
The Minister of the Sea, Jorge Santos, said this Tuesday that the new fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union (EU), approved by the Fisheries Committee of the European Parliament, "was the agreement that was possible".

Government intends to resume dialogue with vessel owners for the creation of an industrial fishing fleet
The government intends to resume dialogue with vessel owners for the creation of an industrial fishing fleet. The information was put forward today by the Minister of the Sea, Abraao Vicente, in reaction to the renewal of the new implementation protocol of the fisheries agreement with the European Union, published this Wednesday.

European Union wants greater communication about the fisheries agreement with Cabo Verde
Cabo Verde has demonstrated knowledge and effectiveness in implementing the fisheries agreement with the European Union, but there is a communication deficit regarding the agreement in the archipelago. This was said by the European Union Ambassador to Cabo Verde, Carla Grijo, who was speaking today on the sidelines of the joint meeting on the fisheries agreement taking place in Sao Vicente.

Government guarantees it is working to avoid new requests for derogation
The European Union has approved a new temporary derogation from the preferential rules of origin, for a period of three years, "but it will probably be the last". The Government guarantees that the necessary investments in the fisheries sector are being made so that the archipelago can comply, within two and a half years, with the rules of origin approved by the European Commission, the relevant ministry announced today.

MEP approves EU/Cabo Verde fisheries agreement but argues for a larger amount
The MEP Claudia Monteiro de Aguiar (PSD) considered that the fisheries agreement between the European Union (EU) and Cabo Verde "results in important support" for the sector, but admitted that it could have been for a higher amount.

Opposition "unaware" of new fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union
The opposition parties with parliamentary seats are not familiar with the new fisheries agreement signed between Cabo Verde and the European Union. Both the PAICV and the UCID state that the document has still not been made available, despite the request made, and that they know only what was presented by the Government.

APESC on the Government's side regarding the new fisheries agreement with the European Union
National vessel owners are giving the Government the benefit of the doubt regarding the new protocol of the fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union. This position was defended today by the president of the Association of Fishing Vessel Owners of Cabo Verde, at a press conference held in Mindelo.

Environmentalists silent on the new fisheries agreement
Environmentalists are not commenting on the new fisheries agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union (EU), signed last Friday. Contacted today by Radio Morabeza, a source from the environmental association Biosfera I said it prefers to remain silent. The same position was taken by the Movement Against Pollution in Cabo Verde.

Environmentalists want an end to shark fishing in the agreement between Cabo Verde and the EU
An environmental movement wants shark fishing to be banned from the agreement between Cabo Verde and the European Union (EU), whose second round of negotiations for a new document is taking place this week, a source from the group told Lusa.

La Nation Bénin...
Une
mission terrain des ambassadeurs de l’Union européenne dans les départements de
la Donga et de l’Atacora était à l’hôpital de zone de Bassila, lundi 13 mai
dernier. La délégation conduite par l’ambassadrice de l’Union européenne au
Bénin, Sylvia Hartleif est allée constater le niveau d’exécution des projets
financés par l’institution dans la zone septentrionale du Bénin, lors de la
semaine de l’Europe tenue du 13 au 17 mai.
Hôpital
de zone de Bassila, première étape de la mission terrain des ambassadeurs de
l’Union européenne lors de la semaine de l’Europe tenue du 13 au 17 mai. Elle
est initiée par l’Union européenne en partenariat avec les ambassades de la
France, des Pays-Bas, de l’Allemagne, de la Belgique et du Luxembourg pour
toucher du doigt les réalisations dans différents secteurs. La délégation
conduite par Sylvia Hartleif, ambassadrice de l’Union européenne au Bénin, a
visité les projets financés par l’institution. L’hôpital de zone de Bassila
bénéficie, grâce à la coopération du Bénin avec la Belgique, d’un financement
pour le projet "Médecins sans vacances" (Msv). 
Dans
ce centre, le projet a permis d’outiller le personnel soignant à travers
des  formations et journées
scientifiques. Le projet a contribué au renforcement des capacités de l'hôpital
de zone de Bassila dans les domaines des urgences obstétricales et néonatales,
la pédiatrie et la gestion hospitalière grâce à l’Ong Médecins sans vacances.
En 2023, le projet a financé la rénovation du service de pédiatrie avec l’appui
de la Coopération belge au développement et aide humanitaire (Dgd) pour offrir
un environnement sain et efficient pour les patients et le staff médical. De la
salle de garde à la néonatologie, en passant par les toilettes, les salles
d’hospitalisation, les urgences, les blocs pédiatriques et la maternité, tous
les compartiments de la pédiatrie ont été réfectionnés. 
Un
abri pour les accompagnants a été érigé en vue d’offrir aux garde-malades de
bonnes conditions de vie. Toutes choses que Abdoulaye Sacca Bawa, directeur de
l’hôpital de zone de Bassila, apprécie. Il informe que de grandes réalisations
ont été faites dans le cadre de l’initiative "Médecins sans vacances"
dont l’acquisition de stérilisateur, d’incinérateur et de concentrateur
d’oxygène. Ces équipements ont permis une réduction significative du taux de
mortalité maternelle et infantile et la prise en charge efficace des femmes et
autres usagers. 
Appréciant
l’impact du projet, Sandrine Platteau, ambassadrice de la Belgique au Bénin,
fait savoir que la santé est la base du développement d’un pays à travers un
bon capital humain. « La délégation est très impressionnée par les réalisations
faites grâce au projet Msv dans cet hôpital. Les chiffres communiqués en termes
de diminution du taux de mortalité maternelle et infantile nous tiennent à
cœur, car ces deux facteurs restent un défi au Bénin», a rappelé la diplomate.
Ces actions révèlent la détermination de l’Union européenne et de ses pays
membres à œuvrer pour des soins de qualité au Bénin. Ceci démontre que la santé
pour tous les citoyens est une priorité de l’Union européenne qui accompagne à
travers des initiatives, le gouvernement.
a6739.en:
La Nation Benin...

A field mission of the ambassadors of the European Union in the departments of Donga and Atacora visited the Bassila zone hospital on Monday 13 May. The delegation, led by the European Union Ambassador to Benin, Sylvia Hartleif, went to observe the level of implementation of the projects financed by the institution in the northern part of Benin, during Europe Week, held from 13 to 17 May.

The Bassila zone hospital was the first stage of the field mission of the European Union ambassadors during Europe Week, held from 13 to 17 May. The week was initiated by the European Union in partnership with the embassies of France, the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium and Luxembourg in order to see at first hand the achievements in various sectors. The delegation led by Sylvia Hartleif, European Union Ambassador to Benin, visited the projects financed by the institution. The Bassila zone hospital benefits, thanks to Benin's cooperation with Belgium, from financing for the "Doctors Without Holidays" (Medecins sans vacances, MSV) project.

At this centre, the project has made it possible to equip the care staff through training sessions and scientific days. The project has contributed to strengthening the capacities of the Bassila zone hospital in the fields of obstetric and neonatal emergencies, paediatrics and hospital management, thanks to the NGO Medecins sans vacances. In 2023, the project financed the renovation of the paediatrics department with the support of Belgian Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid (DGD), in order to offer a healthy and efficient environment for patients and medical staff. From the on-call room to neonatology, by way of the toilets, the wards, the emergency department, the paediatric units and the maternity ward, every part of paediatrics has been refurbished.

A shelter for companions has been built in order to offer carers good living conditions. All of which Abdoulaye Sacca Bawa, director of the Bassila zone hospital, appreciates. He reports that major achievements have been made under the "Medecins sans vacances" initiative, including the acquisition of a steriliser, an incinerator and an oxygen concentrator. This equipment has made possible a significant reduction in the maternal and infant mortality rate and the effective care of women and other users.

Appreciating the impact of the project, Sandrine Platteau, Ambassador of Belgium to Benin, made known that health is the basis of a country's development through good human capital. "The delegation is very impressed by the achievements made thanks to the MSV project in this hospital. The figures communicated in terms of the reduction of the maternal and infant mortality rate are close to our hearts, because these two factors remain a challenge in Benin," the diplomat recalled. These actions reveal the determination of the European Union and its member countries to work for quality care in Benin. This demonstrates that health for all citizens is a priority of the European Union, which supports the government through such initiatives.

a6777.t:
A federal judge ordered the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump to restore funding for hundreds of foreign aid contractors who argued that they were negatively impacted by a 90-day blanket freeze, a court filing showed late on Thursday.
The order temporarily blocks the Trump administration from canceling foreign aid contracts and awards that were in place before Trump took office on January 20.
It was the first such ruling to reverse Trump’s funding freeze on foreign assistance. The ruling came in a lawsuit brought by two health organizations that receive U.S. funding for overseas programs.
Trump has attempted to dismantle government agencies, including the U.S. Agency for International Development, as he has embarked on a massive reshaping of government and has tasked his billionaire ally Elon Musk with cost-cutting.
The stated purpose in suspending of all foreign aid was to provide the opportunity to review programs for their efficiency and consistency with priorities, U.S. District Judge Amir Ali wrote in a filing in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia.
He added: “At least to date, defendants have not offered any explanation for why a blanket suspension of all congressionally appropriated foreign aid, which set off a shockwave and upended reliance interests for thousands of agreements with businesses, nonprofits, and organizations around the country, was a rational precursor to reviewing programs.”
Trump has also ordered agencies to prepare for wide-ranging job cuts, and several have already begun to lay off recent hires who lack full job security.
The Republican has fired and sidelined hundreds of civil servants and top officials at agencies in his first steps toward downsizing the bureaucracy and installing more loyalists.

La Nation Bénin...
L’ambassadeur du Niger près le Bénin, Saadi Abdou, a officiellement lancé, hier jeudi 19 février, au nom du président de la République du Niger, parrain de l’événement, le bouquet panafricain dénommé SeeAfrika. C’était en présence du promoteur, Issa Salifou, du ministre de la Communication Jean Gbéto Dansou et de plusieurs personnalités du monde des médias.
Canal Holding en partenariat avec Eutelsat et Strong, annoncent le démarrage officiel de SeeAfrika, le premier bouquet panafricain pour créer et entretenir les liens entre les Africains du continent et ceux de la diaspora. 
Un démarrage que confirme Jean Jacques Silberstein, directeur général adjoint de Canal 3 Monde qui indique que cela correspond à l’aboutissement de deux ans de travail en France, au Bénin, aux Etats-Unis et au Niger. Pour lui, la philosophie qui sous-tend une telle initiative est de porter un bouquet satellitaire à destination de l’Afrique à partir de l’Afrique.
«Ce sont des difficultés insurmontables que nous sommes en train de surmonter : un vrai challenge par une offre diversifiée, familiale et complète», a indiqué le directeur général adjoint de Canal 3 Monde. Pour lui, le bouquet a été conçu pour offrir un contenu attractif, complet et riche à l’ensemble de la famille africaine où la qualité et le beau priment.
Selon Jean Jacques Silberstein, mis à part le football international, parent pauvre des affiches de SeeAfrika et qui n’est pas une fin en soi, les programmes démarreront vraiment d’ici à la mi-mars simultanément au Bénin, au Niger et au Burkina Faso.
En attendant, la responsable commerciale, Amandine Agonsanou, a fait part du matériel et des différentes offres que SeeAfrika met à la disposition du public. Pour elle, il faut disposer d’une parabole Strong ou Eutelsat de 60 ou 80 cm et souscrire à un abonnement disponible pour deux offres : le bouquet standard avec 10 chaines plus 50 chaines gratuites pour 2500 FCFA par mois et le bouquet intégral qui offre 16 chaines internationales et 50 chaines gratuites pour 9500 FCFA par mois. Pour s'abonner, selon elle, il suffit de se rendre dans un showroom SeeAfrika, d’acheter une carte et se conformer aux conditions et possibilités qui s’offrent au client.
Des conditions et possibilités qui riment bien avec la satisfaction des préoccupations chères au Réseau des instances africaines de régulation de la communication (RIARC) dont le président du Conseil d’administration, Abdourahamane Ousmane, est fier d’assister au démarrage des activités lancées hier jeudi 19 février. Ainsi, entre autres, l’insuffisance des contenus audiovisuels authentiques produits par les Africains pour les Africains, le faible niveau d’échange de contenus africains, la très faible disponibilité de programmes africains, le développement et la consolidation des entreprises médiatiques africaines seront bientôt satisfaites. Sur la base des intérêts mutuellement partagés entre le RIARC et SeeAfrika, la signature d’accord cadre ouvrira la voie à un partenariat fructueux entre le bouquet et les télévisions des pays membres du réseau.
Engagement pour le développement et la réduction de la pauvreté
Le partenariat autour de SeeAfrika réjouit Saadi Abdou, ambassadeur du Niger près le Bénin représentant Mahamadou Issifou, le président de la République nigérienne, parrain de l’événement. Pour elle, l’intérêt du président de la République nigérienne se justifie par son engagement pour le développement et la réduction de la pauvreté. SeeAfrika tient compte des réalités africaines et permet de connecter l’Afrique avec sa diaspora. 
C’est une offre panafricaine qui vise non seulement l’épanouissement de chacun, mais souhaite qu’entre l’Afrique et sa diaspora fleurisse un contact permanent. SeeAfrika emprunte les autoroutes de l’information pour offrir un bouquet panafricain accessible dans le monde entier.
Pour la première fois, une offre planétaire de chaines de télévisions pensée par des Africains et pour des Africains pour une formule améliorée du paysage audiovisuel sera disponible.
SeeAfrika est accessible sous la marque Viewafrika par OTT en France et plus largement en Europe et partout dans le monde. Le bouquet sera visible sur toutes les tablettes numériques Smartphone ainsi que sur les téléviseurs pourvus d’Internet.
Présent au lancement, le ministre de la Communication, Jean Gbéto Dansou, a de très bonnes impressions et pense que SeeAfrika offre la possibilité de suivre les informations sous toutes les formes et qu’il s’agit là d’un bond en avant pour le pays.
Chantal Ahyi, présidente directrice générale de SeeAfrika a offert des paraboles aux officiels qui ont réhaussé la manifestation de leur présence.
a7471.en:
La Nation Benin...

Niger's ambassador to Benin, Saadi Abdou, officially launched yesterday, Thursday 19 February, on behalf of the President of the Republic of Niger, the patron of the event, the pan-African satellite package named SeeAfrika. It took place in the presence of the promoter, Issa Salifou, the Minister of Communication Jean Gbeto Dansou and several personalities from the media world.

Canal Holding, in partnership with Eutelsat and Strong, announce the official start-up of SeeAfrika, the first pan-African package, intended to create and maintain the links between Africans on the continent and those of the diaspora.

A start-up confirmed by Jean Jacques Silberstein, deputy managing director of Canal 3 Monde, who indicates that it corresponds to the culmination of two years of work in France, Benin, the United States and Niger. For him, the philosophy underlying such an initiative is to deliver a satellite package destined for Africa from Africa.

"These are insurmountable difficulties that we are in the process of surmounting: a real challenge through a diversified, family-oriented and complete offering," said the deputy managing director of Canal 3 Monde. For him, the package was designed to offer attractive, complete and rich content to the whole African family, where quality and beauty come first.

According to Jean Jacques Silberstein, apart from international football, the poor relation of SeeAfrika's line-up and not an end in itself, the programmes will really start between now and mid-March, simultaneously in Benin, Niger and Burkina Faso.

In the meantime, the commercial manager, Amandine Agonsanou, reported on the equipment and the various offers that SeeAfrika is making available to the public. In her view, one needs a Strong or Eutelsat satellite dish of 60 or 80 cm and must take out a subscription, available in two offers: the standard package with 10 channels plus 50 free channels for 2,500 CFA francs a month, and the full package which offers 16 international channels and 50 free channels for 9,500 CFA francs a month. To subscribe, according to her, one need only go to a SeeAfrika showroom, buy a card and comply with the conditions and options available to the customer.

Conditions and options that chime well with meeting the concerns dear to the Network of African Communication Regulatory Bodies (RIARC), whose chairman of the board of directors, Abdourahamane Ousmane, is proud to be present at the start of the activities launched yesterday, Thursday 19 February. Thus, among other things, the insufficiency of authentic audiovisual content produced by Africans for Africans, the low level of exchange of African content, the very low availability of African programmes, and the development and consolidation of African media companies will soon be addressed. On the basis of the mutually shared interests between RIARC and SeeAfrika, the signing of a framework agreement will open the way to a fruitful partnership between the package and the television stations of the network's member countries.

Commitment to development and poverty reduction

The partnership around SeeAfrika delights Saadi Abdou, Niger's ambassador to Benin, representing Mahamadou Issifou, the President of the Republic of Niger, the patron of the event. In his view, the interest of the President of the Republic of Niger is justified by his commitment to development and to the reduction of poverty. SeeAfrika takes account of African realities and makes it possible to connect Africa with its diaspora.

It is a pan-African offering that aims not only at the flourishing of each individual, but also hopes that between Africa and its diaspora a permanent contact will blossom. SeeAfrika takes the information highways to offer a pan-African package accessible throughout the world.

For the first time, a global offering of television channels conceived by Africans and for Africans, for an improved formula of the audiovisual landscape, will be available.

SeeAfrika is accessible under the Viewafrika brand by OTT in France and more widely in Europe and everywhere in the world. The package will be viewable on all digital tablets and smartphones as well as on internet-enabled television sets.

Present at the launch, the Minister of Communication, Jean Gbeto Dansou, has very good impressions and thinks that SeeAfrika offers the possibility of following the news in all its forms and that this is a leap forward for the country.

Chantal Ahyi, chief executive officer of SeeAfrika, presented satellite dishes to the officials who honoured the event with their presence.
